questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up, as this may anger them and create more danger.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: On an interstate highway, when must you make a safe lane change?

options.text: When approaching a stopped police vehicle with flashing blue lights.
When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing red lights.
When approaching a stopped maintenance vehicle with flashing amber lights.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to create space when approaching stopped vehicles with flashing lights: blue (police), red (emergency), or amber (maintenance). If you cannot safely change lanes, slow down.

questions.question: What are examples of distractions while driving?

options.text: Music players, cell phones, and GPS devices.
Food and drinks.
Pets moving around in the car.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to use portable electronic devices while driving. Do not eat or drink while driving. Keep pets in carriers to prevent distraction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra travel time.
Obey posted speed limits.
Use proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave plenty of extra time for your trip.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, create a clear path and stop. Pull safely to the right side of the road. In heavy traffic, move slowly to the side until you are out of the way.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the missed exit.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the missed exit.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles using a siren, horn, or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull over to the right side of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through before pulling over.

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. However, when a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer instead of the light.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Cut quickly across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Keep driving and take the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and take the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one instead.

questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Follow other cars instead of the crossing guard.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if no children were around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a crossing guard, sign, or police officer directs you to do so. Always drive with extra caution in school zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A train station is ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of railroad tracks ahead. Always slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Does not affect your driving.
Helps you stay alert.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road, creating danger.

questions.question: To stay alert on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours on long trips to rest and stay alert. If you get drowsy, pull off the road safely and nap, or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway, even with warning labels.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. Always check labels on cold and allergy medicine. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if the drug is safe for driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use headlights from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise.
Using low beam headlights during the day can reduce head-on collisions.
Turn on headlights when snow, rain, or fog reduces visibility.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: By law, use headlights from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise. Drive with low beams on all the time, even during the day, so other drivers see you. Always use headlights in bad weather.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the wheel straight and slow down gradually by releasing the gas.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve side to side to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slow down gradually by releasing the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake until you have control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and pull off the road safely.
